operations.evidence: Firearm and shotgun certificate statistics cover legally held firearms and shotguns only.
The release provides no official estimate of illegally held firearms or shotguns.
The statistics report certificates issued by police forces under the Firearms Act 1968 as amended.
Certificate data do not measure all firearm-related crime or harm.
The data are used to monitor certificates on issue, guns held on certificate and certificate holders.
Monitoring counts are not evidence of risk at a particular address.
A coterminous certificate arrangement aligns the expiry date of a shotgun certificate with a firearm certificate.
Coterminous status does not indicate the number or risk of weapons held.
A firearm certificate lists the number, type and serial number of each weapon and any conditions attached.
Published aggregate statistics do not expose certificate-level serial numbers or conditions.
A shotgun certificate includes descriptions of shotguns and identification numbers where known.
An aggregate shotgun count cannot identify a particular holder or premises.
Police may issue temporary permits in limited circumstances, including delayed renewal processing or estate administration.
A temporary permit should not be treated as a full certificate or as evidence of misconduct.
A visitor's permit can authorise possession without a domestic certificate and cannot exceed 12 months.
Visitor permits do not establish permanent residence or ownership.
Certificates on issue were collected once in 1971 and annually from 1983.
Time-series interpretation must account for gaps and collection changes.
New and renewal applications have been collected annually since 1983.
Application counts are not the same as certificates granted.
Numbers of firearms and shotguns covered by certificates have been collected annually since 1995.
Weapon counts before 1995 are not available on the same basis.
Certificate revocations have been collected annually since 1992.
A revocation count does not reveal the reason or risk associated with a specific case.
Registered firearm dealer statistics have been collected annually since 1995.
Dealer counts do not measure transaction volumes or local firearm prevalence.
Holder age and gender statistics have been collected annually since the year ending March 2016.
The available gender field is limited and missing selections are reported as unknown.
Lost and stolen firearm and shotgun statistics have been collected annually since the year ending March 2021.
The short time series limits long-term comparison.
Temporary permit statistics have been collected since the year ending March 2023.
Early temporary-permit data should be treated as a developing short series.
Certificate statistics are drawn from the live National Firearms Licensing Management System and can change as records are updated.
Extract dates must be preserved when comparing published values.
Home Office statisticians use outlier, variance, plausibility and second-statistician checks with police forces.
Quality assurance does not eliminate all recording and classification errors.
Certificate data for years ending March 2021 and March 2022 were affected by COVID-19 restrictions.
Temporary pandemic effects should not be interpreted as permanent trend shifts.
The move to the national licensing system created limitations around 2006 to 2008, and later data can still contain recording or classification errors.
Series across the system transition require explicit comparability warnings.
